code: fp_richmond <- map_dfr(years, function(yr) {   get_fp(yr) |>     filter(tolower(division) == "richmond") |>     select(year, division, surname, given_name, party, party_name, total_votes) }) # Total formal votes per year (for calculating shares) fp_totals <- fp_richmond |>   group_by(year) |>   summarise(total_formal = sum(total_votes, na.rm = TRUE))  # Major party shares fp_major <- fp_richmond |>   filter(party %in% c("ALP", "NAT", "NP", "LIB", "GRN")) |>   left_join(fp_totals, by = "year") |>   mutate(     pct = round(total_votes / total_formal * 100, 1),     party_label = case_when(       party %in% c("NAT", "NP") ~ "Nationals",       party == "ALP"             ~ "ALP",       party == "LIB"             ~ "Liberal",       party == "GRN"             ~ "Greens",       TRUE                       ~ party     )   ) ggplot(fp_major, aes(x = year, y = pct, colour = party_label)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +   geom_point(size = 2.5) +   scale_colour_manual(values = c(     "ALP"       = "#E4281B",     "Nationals" = "#006644",     "Liberal"   = "#1C4F9C",     "Greens"    = "#10C25B"   )) +   scale_x_continuous(breaks = years) +   scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +   labs(     title   = "Richmond (NSW): first preference vote shares",     x       = NULL,     y       = "First preference share",     colour  = NULL,     caption = "Source: AEC via readaec"   ) +   theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom",         panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

what: 5. How did Richmond swing relative to NSW?
title: Case study: Richmond electorate (2001–2025)
text: Compare Richmond’s election--election swing NSW divisions see whether moved state trend.
code: # Build consecutive election pairs from years with downloads election_pairs <- Map(c, head(years, -1), tail(years, -1))  nsw_swings <- map_dfr(election_pairs, function(pair) {   get_swing(pair[1], pair[2], state = "NSW") |>     filter(!redistribution_flag) |>     mutate(period = paste0(pair[1], "–", pair[2])) }) richmond_swing <- nsw_swings |>   filter(tolower(division) == "richmond") |>   select(period, division, alp_swing, year_from, year_to)  nsw_avg_swing <- nsw_swings |>   group_by(period, year_from, year_to) |>   summarise(avg_alp_swing = mean(alp_swing, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")  swing_comparison <- richmond_swing |>   left_join(nsw_avg_swing, by = c("period", "year_from", "year_to")) |>   mutate(relative_swing = alp_swing - avg_alp_swing)  swing_comparison |>   select(period, richmond_swing = alp_swing, nsw_avg = avg_alp_swing,          relative_swing) #> # A tibble: 6 × 4 #>   period    richmond_swing nsw_avg relative_swing #>   <chr>              <dbl>   <dbl>          <dbl> #> 1 2007–2010          -1.88   -4.56          2.68  #> 2 2010–2013          -4.01   -3.27         -0.739 #> 3 2013–2016           0.98    4.11         -3.13  #> 4 2016–2019           0.12   -1.31          1.43  #> 5 2019–2022           4.15    3.14          1.01  #> 6 2022–2025           1.77    3.97         -2.20 swing_comparison |>   select(period, richmond_swing = alp_swing, nsw_avg = avg_alp_swing) |>   tidyr::pivot_longer(c(richmond_swing, nsw_avg),                       names_to = "series", values_to = "swing") |>   mutate(series = if_else(series == "richmond_swing", "Richmond", "NSW average")) |>   ggplot(aes(x = period, y = swing, fill = series)) +   geom_col(position = "dodge") +   geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey40") +   scale_fill_manual(values = c("Richmond" = "#E4281B", "NSW average" = "grey70")) +   scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(ifelse(x > 0, "+", ""), x, "pp")) +   labs(     title   = "Richmond ALP swing vs NSW average",     x       = NULL,     y       = "ALP swing (percentage points)",     fill    = NULL,     caption = "Source: AEC via readaec"   ) +   theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom",         axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),         panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

title: Access Australian Electoral Commission Data
text: Australian Electoral Commission publishes detailed results every federal election tally room results.aec.gov.au. elections 2007 onwards, includes first preference votes, two-party preferred, two-candidate preferred, booth-level results, polling place coordinates, Senate counts, enrolment, turnout - available CSV downloads updated live election night. catch election URL structure built around internal event ID, column names shift years without warning, API. Getting data requires knowing right URL pattern, handling inconsistencies across elections, writing fresh code every time. readaec wraps AEC’s CSV downloads consistent, tidy interface. One function call returns clean data frame. Results cached locally ’re hitting AEC’s servers every call. covers federal elections 2007 2025 (including Senate), House -elections 2008 2026 Farrer -election, 2023 referendum.

title: Access Australian Electoral Commission Data
text: readaec covers federal elections 2007 onwards. everything outside scope, ’s look. Federal elections, 2001–2022: eechidna bundles House Representatives results 2001 2022 ready--use R data frames. standout feature census join - ABS demographic variables apportioned electoral boundaries - making best option socio-economic analysis Howard--Morrison era. doesn’t cover Senate stops 2022. readaec eechidna complementary rather competing. Federal elections, pre-2001: AEC provides ZIP archives 1993, 1996, 1998 elections via statistics download page, packaged legacy fixed-width files - usable pleasant. anything earlier, Adam Carr’s Psephos archive canonical source, covering federal results back 1901 plain-text format. David Barry done hard work combining Psephos AEC digital records cleaner, analysis-friendly series 1901 present. Federal state elections: Tally Room - run psephologist Ben Raue - covers federal state elections across Australian jurisdictions, plus New Zealand. Ben publishes clean booth-level CSVs lat/lon coordinates consistent format, going back roughly 2001. Recent elections free; historical back-catalogue available via Patreon. key difference readaec Ben’s federal data manually curated published static files, whereas readaec pulls live AEC - making readaec better suited programmatic access current results. state territory elections, Ben’s data essentially structured source exists.

title: readaec 0.2.0
text: -election support: list_by_elections() plus get_by_election_fp(), get_by_election_tcp(), get_by_election_tpp(), get_by_election_candidates(). Covers 24 House -elections AEC CSV downloads, Gippsland 2008 Farrer 2026. Referendum support: list_referendums(), get_referendum_by_booth(), get_referendum_turnout() 2023 Voice referendum, including booth-level Yes/counts. get_dop() returns full count--count distribution preferences division, dataset needed analyse seats won behind preference flows. get_tcp_by_booth() returns two-candidate preferred votes polling place. get_senators_elected() returns senators elected order election.

title: readaec 0.2.0
text: get_swing() now reports party actually won seat (winner_from, winner_to), joined AEC members elected file. Previously winners inferred TPP shares, misidentified seats won independents minor parties. TPP-based columns retained tpp_leader_from tpp_leader_to. data functions gain refresh argument force re-download, useful election night cached counts go stale. HTTP failures now produce readable error status code. Previously status check unreachable ‘httr2’ errors non-200 responses check ran. Downloads written temporary file moved cache complete, interrupted download can longer leave corrupt file served cache indefinitely. Requests now identify package via user agent retry three times transient failures. Column types now guessed whole file rather first 1000 rows, fixing parsing warnings get_polling_places().
